# Healthcare Performance Indicators

This folder groups supplementary national quality indicators from the Danish Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) that evaluate the speed of surgical interventions for acute patients. The pages within track time-to-surgery benchmarks for both life-threatening conditions, such as perforation, ischemia, or bleeding, and non-life-threatening acute cases. Together, they document systemic capacity challenges, widespread failure to meet strict six-hour operation targets, and significant regional and hospital-level disparities in acute surgical triage across Denmark.

## Pages

- [[indikator-5x|Indikator 5x]] — Measures the proportion of acute surgical patients with life-threatening conditions operated on within six hours, revealing a national compliance rate of only 21.2% against a 90% standard.
- [[indikator-5y|Indikator 5y]] — Tracks the speed of acute surgical treatment for patients without life-threatening conditions, documenting a national compliance rate of just 14.7% for the six-hour target window.
